title: POC Weekly Sync - App integration / SDK + structured output - Arcadia Labs

header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Time: 15:00 PT (PST)
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (Arcadia PM), Diego Ramos (Arcadia Lead Eng), Sofia Alvarez (Arcadia Security)
Meeting ID: ff-20260916-arcadia-poc-sync-03
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick roll call, Ravi and I from Redwood, and Arcadia team?
[00:06] Laura Kim: Laura here.
[00:08] Diego Ramos: Diego.
[00:09] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia on security.
[00:11] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today is: SDK integration status, results from structured-output tests, and agree on next steps for the pilot run.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: I'll start with the SDK notes — we pushed the Node and Python snippets to the shared drive, but Diego you mentioned some parsing errors last week?
[00:28] Diego Ramos: yeah, so when we trigger tool calls from the app the function payload comes back in a slightly different shape than our parser expects, example the Redwood output uses "tool_response" vs our parser looking for "result" — small mismatch, but causes the pipeline to drop items.
[00:40] Maya Chen: got it, that's usually mapping config; we have a sample mapping layer we can share. Are these results from the streaming responses or the post-response payload?
[00:48] Diego Ramos: mainly streaming, we tried both. Streaming chunks sometimes split the JSON object across multiple messages so our naive JSON parse fails.
[00:56] Ravi Patel: that's a known gotcha — our streaming SDK has example code to buffer and reassemble full structured outputs, plus a mode to emit complete JSON object messages when you set streaming.mode = "json_chunks" — I'll drop the snippet.
[01:10] Laura Kim: ok that would help. also some of the function calls returned with extra metadata fields we didn't expect, like kv_cache_hit: true, which broke our validation.
[01:19] Maya Chen: yes some SDKs include metadata; we can show you how to strip or map those server-side. question — are you validating against a strict JSON schema or using a tolerant parser?
[01:29] Diego Ramos: strict, we want deterministic fields: id, claim_text, normalized_amount, categories[], source_id.
[01:36] Sofia Alvarez: and security side — we need to ensure PII fields are redacted before logs leave Arcadia — is Redwood able to run pre-emit hooks or do local redaction?
[01:45] Ravi Patel: for Private and Dedicated customers we support pre-send hooks and local redaction; for hosted we recommend client-side redaction or using our PII redaction pipeline. We also support KMS integrations so you can keep payloads encrypted in transit and at rest.
[01:56] Sofia Alvarez: good. can you confirm that rotation is supported and that audit logs include per-request key id?
[02:01] Maya Chen: yes — audit logs include key identifiers and request metadata; we'll include the SOC 2 appendix for the pilot.
[02:08] Laura Kim: great. on accuracy — we ran the summary model on 200 claims, precision for normalized_amount is around 92% but sometimes misses currency conversion.
[02:18] Ravi Patel: are you passing a canonical currency field or expecting model to infer? if you provide explicit currency_hint we can route to a model profile tuned for multi-currency.
[02:27] Diego Ramos: we generally expect inference to normalize if there's no currency field; but ok we'll try passing currency_hint. is there a cost/latency tradeoff?
[02:34] Maya Chen: slightly — models that do heavy normalization might increase token usage; we can show per-token breakdown in the console and recommend batching for the ingestion step to lower unit cost.
[02:44] Ravi Patel: speaking of batching, Diego, you mentioned earlier the batcher timed out on some 40-document batches?
[02:50] Diego Ramos: right — our load is spiky, sometimes the batch window fills slowly and we hit latency SLOs.
[02:55] Ravi Patel: you can lower batch window and increase concurrency, or pin you to a dedicated pool for more predictable throughput. For the pilot we can simulate your spike pattern and tune autoscale policy.
[03:06] Laura Kim: what's the difference in cost between using hosted with autoscale vs Dedicated? ballpark.
[03:12] Maya Chen: hosted is usage-based, good for variable loads; Dedicated is commit-based and is more predictable and lower cost per token at scale. I'll attach a comparison.
[03:20] Sofia Alvarez: back to security — what about egress control and VPC peering?
[03:24] Maya Chen: for Dedicated and Private we support VPC peering and strict egress rules, plus we can run the control plane in a customer VPC for Private deployments.
[03:33] Diego Ramos: ok interesting. now on structured output: we saw 12 failures out of 200 where the model emitted a different field type — categories came back as a string instead of array.
[03:44] Ravi Patel: this usually correlates with temperature or prompt conditioning — we recommend zero-shot with explicit schema examples, and use function-calling where possible because function outputs are more strictly typed.
[03:54] Maya Chen: also consider using the structured-output mode in the SDK which enforces schema compliance and can surface parse errors as part of the response so you can retry.
[04:03] Diego Ramos: can you show a quick example of function calling + structured output?
[04:07] Ravi Patel: yeah, I'll share a snippet, but briefly: define a function signature with expected params (categories: array[string], normalized_amount: number) and call the function via SDK. The runtime will return a typed payload, and if it doesn't match, you'll get an error field.
[04:19] Laura Kim: will that error be retriable or do we have to fallback to a secondary model?
[04:23] Ravi Patel: you can set automatic fallback rules — e.g., on schema failure call a conservative model variant with deterministic decoding, or run a repair prompt to fix the JSON.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: hmm repair prompts sound like extra steps; we'd prefer deterministic outputs.
[04:36] Maya Chen: for deterministic you can lower temperature and use model variants that have been quantized and tuned for reliability — we can recommend a quantization profile that keeps accuracy high while improving cost.
[04:46] Sofia Alvarez: will quantization affect auditability or change the output formats that we rely on?
[04:51] Ravi Patel: not the format; quantization mainly affects model weights and perf characteristics. outputs should remain the same format-wise; we do recommend running a small eval to check for regression.
[05:00] Laura Kim: ok. Diego, any blockers on your side for running the 1k batch we discussed?
[05:04] Diego Ramos: just need the SDK snippet for streaming + function calls and the schema mapping example; plus we'll need sample logs to test our redaction pipeline.
[05:12] Maya Chen: we'll provide those. Also, Sofia requested audit-log samples which we will attach from our compliance pack.
[05:19] Sofia Alvarez: thanks. also want to verify that you can support HSM-backed keys for the pilot?
[05:24] Ravi Patel: yes we support HSM via KMS partner integrations — we'll list supported providers in the security appendix.
[05:31] Laura Kim: quick note on infra — our app runs in GCP us-central1, do you have regional Dedicated capacity there?
[05:37] Maya Chen: we do have Dedicated pools in us-central1; we can route traffic regionally for latency.
[05:42] Diego Ramos: for the benchmark run, can we run both hosted and Dedicated and compare P50/P95 latencies?
[05:47] Maya Chen: yes, we can run side-by-side benchmarks. we'll need a representative workload.
[05:52] Ravi Patel: if you send us request traces we can replay them into the benchmark harness and return a CSV with token cost and latency percentiles.
[05:59] Laura Kim: Diego will prepare that.
[06:02] Diego Ramos: yep. noted.
[06:04] [06:06] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:08] Maya Chen: ok next topic: observability — you asked about token-level cost and trace mapping?
[06:15] Laura Kim: yes, specifically per-endpoint and per-route breakdowns so we can attribute cost to different features.
[06:21] Ravi Patel: Console provides per-route, per-model and per-token breakdowns and you can export to BigQuery or S3. we'll share a dashboard template.
[06:30] Sofia Alvarez: what's the retention on logs for audit? we may need 12 months.
[06:35] Maya Chen: audit logs retention for Dedicated/Private is configurable; hosted has default 90 days but we offer add-on retention.
[06:43] Diego Ramos: any gotchas on SDK versions? we saw a deprecation warning in logs.
[06:48] Ravi Patel: ensure you're on SDK v3.2.1 or later — older versions had a streaming protocol change. I'll include the compatibility matrix.
[06:56] Laura Kim: good.
[07:00] Maya Chen: let's recap immediate deliverables: SDK snippets for streaming + function calls (Ravi), JSON schema mapping examples and mapping layer suggestions (Ravi/Maya), updated pricing + pilot runbook (Maya), sample audit logs and KMS/HSM appendix (Maya), customer to run 1k batch and produce traces (Diego).
[07:18] Diego Ramos: timeline: we can run the 1k batch by Monday 2026-09-21, as long as we get the snippets today.
[07:25] Maya Chen: we'll send snippets by EOD 2026-09-16.
[07:28] Laura Kim: we'll aim for the Monday run.
[07:30] Sofia Alvarez: I'll review the KMS appendix and get back with any additional requirements by next Wednesday.
[07:36] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[07:39] Diego Ramos: one quick thing — do you support tool-calling that can reach out to our internal enrichment service via a webhook? we want the model to call a tool that fetches exchange rates.
[07:48] Ravi Patel: yes, function/tool calling supports webhooks and secure signing; you can register a tool endpoint and the runtime will call it during the request lifecycle. we recommend signed webhook tokens and short TTLs.
[07:58] Laura Kim: excellent. that should fix currency conversion issues.
[08:01] Maya Chen: ok thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. bye for now.
[08:05] Laura Kim: thanks bye.
[08:07] Diego Ramos: bye.
[08:08] Sofia Alvarez: bye.
